title: Minit Records and Art Rupe's hidden ownership of A1 Distributors
summary: Minit was the most successful local label; Banashak was cheated when Art Rupe, who financed A1, would not let him buy him out.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: But it seems to me that Joe was the first, when he formed Minute Records, that was really the first serious record company, seems to me, here in the city, really. I mean, correct me.
No, not really. There were some efforts before that.
Maybe his became the most successful.

Oh, yes. No question about it. And the original Minute Records had a couple of partners who were partners by virtue of their ability to get records played, as opposed to participating either in the capitalization or the operation of the company.
Who were the partners, Steve?
One of them's obvious, Larry McKinley.
Well, I knew Larry McKinley, but I thought maybe some others that I...

Well, I don't know for sure. A couple of minor players. Not minor players in the sense of who they were, but minor players on the business side of it. But to get back to what we were talking about, Joe finally succumbed to his understanding, his understanding that he'd been immensely cheated by a couple of major players. Art Roup, primarily.
Lou Chiod, I think is...
No, no. Art Roup. Yeah. A1 Distributors was owned by Art Roup surreptitiously.
You mean Joe's A1 Distributors was owned?
Right. By Art Roup. And...
In other words, Joe...
Joe... Joe...
Joe worked for Art?
In that sense, yes. But... In the... The understanding was that Joe would buy Art out completely as they went along. Mm-hmm. And Art didn't let him.
Mm-hmm.

You know, Art didn't let him. Art didn't live up to his end of the thing. Now, he... I guess he's still alive. I would probably say that's not true. But I understood it to be true in just casual conversation over the years with them, you know.
So when... And then we back up. When Joe found... Joe, from what I understood, founded A1...
Mm-hmm. He had the financial backing of Art Roup.
Yeah, Roup gave him the financing.
Roup put up the money.
Right. To...

Right. To get A1. And literally owned it legally. Mm-hmm. And they had some paperwork that said that this portion of it is Joe Banaszak's and this other portion of it he can buy and all that. But Art Roup managed to finesse Joe out of all that. Mm-hmm. And that was the one thing. The other major disappointment he had was, of course, that... That... He lost Alan Toussaint.
